chapter: Reel IV retellings and New York pianists
title: Joe Steele, the conservatory pianist, and Gershwin at the Lafayette
summary: He describes Boston pianist Joe Steele, nine years at the Conservatory, who played Rhapsody in Blue at the Lafayette, where Gershwin kissed him.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Was there a guy around here named Steel? Was he a piano player or a drummer?
Joe Steele.
Was he a piano player?
He played for Chick Webb.
He was a piano player, though, right?
From Boston.
He's another one from Boston, huh?
That's right. Joe Steele was a conservatory man. He and I went to the conservatory together, and I quit -- but he stayed there. He was in the conservatory nine years.
Uh huh.
And boy, he could tell you why that was F flat and why you go to B flat, like that.
That's him, yeah. And he had a gold tooth in his mouth, didn't he?
I don't know about that, I don't remember. But anyway ...
And a good dresser, right?

Yeah, he used to tell me he wanted to get out of -- he didn't like playing, and I'd say, "Well, why don't you quit? A man of your talent, shish..." He played Rhapsody in Blue, and what's the guy's name who wrote it?
George Gershwin.
George Gershwin jumped on the stage and kissed him after he got through playing it.
Is that so? Where was that at?
At the Lafayette Theatre.
Lafayette Theatre.
Yeah.
